normalIntro.en: These memories go through the adjective behind the adverb, its suffix, and its frequent partners.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条通过副词背后的形容词、它的后缀与常见搭配来记。

normal.en: Tightly is tight plus -ly, so learn the adjective and the adverb follows.
normal.cn: tightly 是 tight 加 -ly，记住形容词，副词自然跟上。

normal.en: Hold tightly is the most natural partner: grip the verb and the adverb together.
normal.cn: hold tightly 是最自然的搭配：把动词和副词一起记。

normal.en: Tightly packed is the crowds-and-cargo phrase of the word.
normal.cn: tightly packed 是这个词用于人群与货物的短语。

normal.en: Tightly controlled shows the same adverb serving rules rather than ropes.
normal.cn: tightly controlled 显示同一个副词也能用于规则而非绳子。

normal.en: The adverb never becomes tightlier; only the adjective takes -er and -est.
normal.cn: 这个副词不能写成 tightlier，只有形容词才有比较级和最高级。

abstract.en: Picture a sailor's hands pulling a rope until the veins stand up.
abstract.cn: 想象水手把绳子拉到青筋凸起。

abstract.en: Think of a jam jar closed by someone stronger than you, and the lid will not turn.
abstract.cn: 想一只被人用力拧紧的果酱罐，盖子纹丝不动。

abstract.en: A tightly knit village is a net whose knots sit close together.
abstract.cn: 紧密团结的村庄就是一张结子挨得很近的网。

examples.en: He held the railing tightly as the ship rolled.
examples.cn: 船身摇晃时他死死抓住栏杆。

examples.en: The box was tightly packed with old letters.
examples.cn: 箱子里塞满了旧信件。

examples.en: Her eyes were tightly closed against the bright sun.
examples.cn: 她的眼睛紧紧闭着，躲避刺眼的阳光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太特利」——绳子捆得太特别利索，一点缝都没留。

root: 由形容词 tight（古英语 thight，密集的）加本土副词后缀 -ly 构成，词义史随形容词，无独立来源。

sensesIntro.en: Every use of the adverb is one shade of the same picture: no slack, whether in grip, closure, packing, rules, schedules, results, or closed eyes.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词的每种用法都是同一幅图的一种色调：无论握持、闭合、堆积、规则、日程、结果还是闭眼，都是「没有余量」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grip or a closure with zero slack anywhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次握持或一次闭合，处处没有余量。

branches.en: Firm holding and complete closing of the body.
branches.cn: 牢固握持与身体的完全闭合。

branches.en: Sealing a space against outside air or dust.
Packing in space and in time.
branches.cn: 在空间与时间上的挤满。

branches.en: Strict control and close human bonds.
branches.cn: 严格控制与紧密的人间纽带。

branches.en: A contest with almost no gap between sides.
branches.cn: 双方几乎没有差距的竞争。

intro.en: The affix work here is the productive -ly ending, which is added to an adjective that already carries the whole meaning.
intro.cn: 这里的构词要点是能产的 -ly 结尾，它加在一个已承载全部意义的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: Tightly has no Latin etymon; the borrowed Latin items below are offered only as semantic parallels.
latinIntro.cn: tightly 没有拉丁词源；下面借入的拉丁词仅作语义对照。

items.example: The whole meaning belongs to this base.
items.exampleCN: 全部意义都落在这个词基上。

items.example: It marks tightly as an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它使 tightly 成为副词。

items.example: The ending was itself once an adjective form.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾本身也曾经是形容词形式。

items.example: Tightly-knit is a common compound.
Tighten keeps the making sense.
Tightness is the noun.
The adjective, not the adverb, takes it.
items.exampleCN: 只有形容词可用，副词不可。

items.example: Tightest belongs to the adjective.

definition_zh: 直到；在……以前；耕种；耕作；钱柜；抽屉
definition_en: up to a stated time; also to prepare land for crops by ploughing, and a drawer for money in a shop
core_image: 犁头翻开土壤，一直推到田埂的尽头
scene: 春寒刚退，田里还留着去年的秸秆。The farmers began to till the fields as soon as the frost left the ground.
sceneCN: 这里 till 是「耕种」（第 3 个义项：翻耕土地准备播种）；句意为霜一落地就散了，农民开始翻耕田地。画面里有犁、湿土与田垄。

pos.zh: 介词：直到……
连词：直到……为止
动词：耕种、耕作
名词：钱柜；抽屉

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -age 构成，义为「耕作；耕地」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「耕作者」或「舵柄」
加否定前缀 un- 与过去分词结尾构成，义为「未耕的；荒芜的」

senses.title: Up to a point in time
senses.definition: up to a particular time and no further
senses.definitionCN: 一直延续到某一时间，不再往后
senses.example: The shop stays open till nine on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店周五营业到九点。
senses.why: The Old English form held the idea of reaching a limit, and time is the limit most often reached.
senses.whyCN: 古英语形式含有「抵达界限」之意，而时间是最常被抵达的界限。

senses.title: As a conjunction before an event
senses.definition: used before a clause describing the event that ends a period
senses.definitionCN: 用在从句前，表示结束一段时间的事件
senses.example: Wait here till the rain stops.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里等到雨停。
senses.why: The same limit is now a moment marked by an event rather than a clock.
senses.whyCN: 同样的界限此时由一个事件、而不是钟点来标记。

senses.title: To plough and prepare land
senses.definition: to prepare land for growing crops by ploughing and working the soil
senses.definitionCN: 通过翻耕与整地准备庄稼用地
senses.example: They tilled the soil in long straight furrows.
senses.exampleCN: 他们翻出长长笔直的地垄。
senses.why: This homonym is a separate Old English verb meaning to strive for or work at, and farming became its main field.
senses.whyCN: 这是另一个古英语动词的同一拼写，意为「努力争取、劳作」，农事成为其主要领域。

senses.title: A drawer for money
senses.definition: a drawer or small machine that holds money in a shop
senses.definitionCN: 商店里存放钱款的抽屉或小型机器
senses.example: She counted the coins in the till at closing time.
senses.exampleCN: 打烊时她清点了钱柜里的硬币。
senses.why: The container seems to be named from the drawer that was drawn out and held, and the origin is debated.
senses.whyCN: 这个容器一般被认为得名于可拉出并存放东西的抽屉，但确切来源尚有争论。

senses.title: A tiller of the soil
senses.definition: used in the phrase tiller of the soil for a farmer
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 tiller of the soil，指农夫
senses.example: He has been a tiller of the soil all his life.
senses.exampleCN: 他一辈子都在耕种土地。
senses.why: The verb plus -er gives the person who works the land, a settled farming identity.
senses.whyCN: 动词加 -er 得到经营土地的人，是一种固定的农人身份。

senses.title: Till then, an expected time
senses.definition: in the phrase till then, meaning up to a future point already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 用于 till then，表示直到前面提到的将来某时
senses.example: We will keep the seat empty till then.
senses.exampleCN: 到那时为止我们会把座位空着。
senses.why: The limit sense is fixed in a short phrase that points forward to a named moment.
senses.whyCN: 界限义固定在指向某个已知时刻的短语里。

senses.title: Not till, a delayed action
senses.definition: used with not to show that an action happened only at a late point
senses.definitionCN: 与 not 连用，表示动作到很晚才发生
senses.example: He did not answer till the second letter arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 直到第二封信到，他才回复。
senses.why: Here the limit is reached late, so the verb waiting for it is delayed as well.
senses.whyCN: 这里界限到得晚，等待它的动词也跟着推迟。

senses.title: Until a place or distance
senses.definition: used in older or dialectal English for up to a place or distance
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧或方言英语中表示延伸到某处或某段距离
senses.example: The lane runs till the old mill.
senses.exampleCN: 这条小路一直通到老磨坊。
senses.why: From time the limit sense extends to space, where a lane can also reach its end.
senses.whyCN: 界限义从时间延伸到空间，小路也能抵达终点。

intro.en: Two different Old English words lie behind the modern form: one marking a limit in time, the other meaning to work at or strive for. The money drawer is a third and uncertain story.
intro.cn: 现代拼写背后有两个不同的古英语词：一个标记时间界限，一个意为「劳作、努力」；钱柜则是第三段来源不明的故事。

items.en: The preposition til meant up to, related to the idea of a goal reached.
items.cn: 介词 til 意为「直到」，与「抵达目标」的观念相关。

items.en: A separate verb tilian meant to strive for, work at, or cultivate.
items.cn: 另一个动词 tilian 意为努力争取、从事或耕作。

items.en: The Old Norse til also meant to or up to, and reinforced the preposition in the north.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 til 也意为「到」，在北方强化了这个介词。

items.en: The two words fall together in spelling, and the farming sense dominates the verb.
items.cn: 这两个词拼写合并，耕作义成为动词的主义。

items.en: The shop till is attested from the end of the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 商店钱柜义在十七世纪末见于记载。

items.en: Scholars still debate whether the money till is related to the verb or to a separate noun for a drawn-out drawer.
items.cn: 学者仍在争论钱柜义是与这个动词有关，还是与另一个指可拉出抽屉的名词有关。

note.en: The look-alike group handles the easily confused pair till and until, and the near-meaning group gathers other limit and farming words.
note.cn: 形近组处理容易混淆的 till 与 until，近义组收集表示界限与耕作的其他词。

entries.definition: up to a stated time, the fuller form of till
one who tills land, or a handle for steering
the work of preparing land for crops
to lean to one side, a different word
entries.definitionCN: 倾斜；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to prepare and use land for crops
to turn over soil with a blade
a machine that holds and records money in a shop
from a point in the past up to now

normalIntro.en: These memories separate the three lives of the spelling: time limit, farming, and the money drawer.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条把同一拼写的三重身份分开记：时间界限、耕作与钱柜。

normal.en: Till the time word and until share a root; till is the shorter everyday form.
normal.cn: till 与 until 同源，till 是更短的口语形式。

normal.en: Not till puts not before the limit, so the action waits for the deadline.
normal.cn: not till 把否定放在界限前，动作因此等到最后。

normal.en: The farming till is a separate Old English verb tilian, meaning to work at.
normal.cn: 耕作义的 till 来自另一个古英语动词 tilian，意为「劳作」。

normal.en: Tillage and tiller both grow from the farming verb.
normal.cn: tillage 与 tiller 都由耕作动词长出。

normal.en: The shop till is a drawer, so picture coins in a pulled-out box by the counter.
normal.cn: 商店的 till 是抽屉，想象柜台边拉出的盒子里放着硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a road that stops exactly at a gate and goes no further.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路正好停在一道门前，再没有延伸。

abstract.en: Think of a plough cutting a dark line to the far edge of a field.
abstract.cn: 想犁头在田里划出一道直到地头的黑线。

abstract.en: A till drawer slides out smoothly when the sale is made.
abstract.cn: 售出一笔，钱屉就顺畅地滑出来。

examples.en: We waited till the last bus had gone.
examples.cn: 我们一直等到末班车开走。

examples.en: The family tills a small plot behind the house.
examples.cn: 这家人在屋后耕种一小块地。

examples.en: She put the notes in the till and locked the shop.
examples.cn: 她把纸币放进钱柜，然后锁了店门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提尔」——一直提到田的最尽头，才算耕完。

root: 时间义的 till 来自古英语 til（直到）并受古诺斯语 til 强化；耕作义的 till 来自古英语 tilian（劳作、耕作）；商店钱柜义来源不确定，一般认为与可拉出的抽屉有关。

sensesIntro.en: The entry follows two clear lines and one uncertain one: the limit in time and space, the working of land, and the money drawer that has no settled origin.
sensesIntro.cn: 本词涵盖两条清楚的线索和一条不明线索：时间与空间上的界限、土地的耕作，以及来源尚定的钱柜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line pushed forward until it reaches its exact end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条线向前推进，直到抵达确切的尽头。

branches.en: The time limit and the phrases that fix it.
branches.cn: 时间界限以及固定它的短语。

branches.en: The limit transferred to space.
Working land to its edge.
The drawer that slides out to its stop.
The everyday short form beside until.
branches.cn: 与 until 并列的日常短形式。

intro.en: The spelling carries two Old English stems, so the affix work shows the endings that build its noun and person forms.
intro.cn: 这个拼写承载两个古英语词干，因此构词要点是构成名词与人物形式的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Nothing Latin lies behind either stem; the Latin list holds only parallel words for tillage and for boundaries.
latinIntro.cn: 两个词干背后都没有拉丁语；拉丁表只列耕作与边界的对照词。

items.example: The time sense belongs to this root.
The farming sense belongs to this verb.
Tillage names the work of tilling.
Tiller names the farmer.
Untilled land has not been worked.
Tilled soil is ready for seed.
Tills serves as noun plural and verb form.
items.exampleCN: tills 既是复数也是动词形式。

items.example: Tilling keeps the soil loose.

definition_zh: 木材；木料；树木；横梁；（人的）素质
definition_en: wood prepared for building or carpentry, standing trees grown for that use, or a large beam in a structure
core_image: 堆放整齐的粗木方，锯口还带着新鲜木屑
scene: 新工地刚清完场地，卡车把成捆的木料卸在角落。Workers stacked the timber under a tarpaulin to keep it dry.
sceneCN: 这里 timber 是「木材、木料」（第 1 个义项：供建筑或木工用的木料）；句意为工人们把木料堆在防水布下防潮。画面里有木方、锯屑与工地角落。

pos.zh: 名词：木材、木料；树木；横梁；人的素质

derivatives.zh: 加过去分词结尾，义为「木造的；有木材的」
加 -ing 名词化，义为「木支架；木材结构」
复合词，义为「木材场」

senses.title: Wood cut for building
senses.definition: wood that has been cut and prepared for use in building or carpentry
senses.definitionCN: 已锯好备用的建筑或木工用木材
senses.example: The barn was built from local timber.
senses.exampleCN: 这间谷仓是用本地的木材盖的。
senses.why: The Old English word first named a building or a structure, then the material that such structures were made from.
senses.whyCN: 古英语最初指建筑物、构造物，随后指建造这类构造所用的材料。

senses.title: Standing trees as a crop
senses.definition: forest trees considered as a resource to be harvested
senses.definitionCN: 被视为可采伐资源的森林树木
senses.example: The hillside timber was felled over one winter.
senses.exampleCN: 山坡上的林木在一个冬天里被砍伐。
senses.why: If cut wood is timber, then the trees waiting to be cut are timber too.
senses.whyCN: 如果锯下的木头是木材，那么等待被锯的树也算木材。

senses.title: A heavy beam
senses.definition: a large piece of shaped wood used as a beam in a structure
senses.definitionCN: 结构中用作梁的巨大木料
senses.example: One timber in the roof had rotted through.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶上有一根横梁已经烂穿。
senses.why: A beam is the cut wood at its most structural, carrying the weight of the building.
senses.whyCN: 横梁是木料最具结构性的形态，承担着建筑的重量。

senses.title: Wooden supports for a mine
senses.definition: the wooden props used to support tunnels in a mine
senses.definitionCN: 矿井中支撑巷道的木质支柱
senses.example: They set new timber against the tunnel walls.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在巷道两壁架上新的木支架。
senses.why: Underground, the same beam sense becomes a safety structure holding back falling ground.
senses.whyCN: 在地下，同样的横梁义变成了挡住塌方的安全结构。

senses.title: Personal qualities
senses.definition: used figuratively for the qualities from which a person is made
senses.definitionCN: 比喻人的素质、禀性
senses.example: The coach saw good timber in the young player.
senses.exampleCN: 教练看出这个年轻球员是块好料。
senses.why: To build something well you need good timber, so a person worth building is said to be good timber.
senses.whyCN: 要做好东西就得用好木材，于是值得造就的人也被说成好木材。

senses.title: Land covered with trees
senses.definition: forest land, especially in a phrase such as timber land
senses.definitionCN: 森林用地，尤见于 timber land 等短语
senses.example: The family owns a few acres of timber land.
senses.exampleCN: 这家拥有几英亩林地。
senses.why: Land that grows the material takes on the name of the material it produces.
senses.whyCN: 生长这种材料的土地被冠上了它所产材料的名字。

senses.title: The call that a tree is falling
senses.definition: the warning shout given when a felled tree is about to fall
senses.definitionCN: 伐倒的树将要倒下时发出的警告呼喊
senses.example: Timber went up from the far end of the clearing.
senses.exampleCN: 林间空地另一头传来「倒树了」的喊声。
senses.why: The warning names the material as it comes down, so the word becomes the shout itself.
senses.whyCN: 这声警告喊的正是落下的材料，于是词本身成了呼喊。

senses.title: A heavy usable frame
senses.definition: used for a strong person or structure that supports others
senses.definitionCN: 喻指能支撑他人的强壮的人或结构
senses.example: He was a timber of the party, steady through every crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 他是党内的一根栋梁，每次危机中都稳得住。
senses.why: A beam holds up a roof, so a person who holds up a group is compared to that beam.
senses.whyCN: 横梁撑起屋顶，撑起团体的人便被比作横梁。

intro.en: The word appears in Old English as timber, first naming a building, and Old Norse timberr carries the same senses of building and building material.
intro.cn: 这个词在古英语中作 timber，最初指建筑物；古诺斯语 timberr 同样兼有「建筑物」与「建材」两义。

items.en: Timber named a building, a structure that gives shelter.
items.cn: timber 指建筑物，即提供遮蔽的构造物。

items.en: Timberr also meant building material and influenced the northern forms.
items.cn: timberr 也指建筑材料，影响了北方各方言的形式。

items.en: The sense of wood prepared for building becomes dominant.
items.cn: 「备好的建筑用木材」这一义项成为主导。

items.en: The word extends to beams and to standing trees grown for timber.
items.cn: 本词扩展到横梁以及专为木材而种的树木。

items.en: Mining and shipbuilding give the word fixed technical senses as a support.
items.cn: 采矿与造船给本词固定的技术义：「支撑木」。

items.en: The figurative good timber and the lumberjack shout are both in common use.
items.cn: 比喻义的「好料」与伐木工的呼喊现都通用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words for pieces of wood, and the near-meaning group collects the building and forest vocabulary around this one.
note.cn: 形近组收集各类木料的词，近义组则聚集与木材相近的建筑与森林词汇。

entries.definition: built with timber, as of a house
wooden supports used in a shaft or tunnel
a yard where timber is stored and sold
the quality of a musical sound
entries.definitionCN: 音色；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: timber sawn into planks, especially in American use
entries.definitionCN: 木材；美式用法指锯好的木板

entries.definition: a long piece of wood or metal that supports a structure
a thick piece of cut tree trunk
a long flat piece of sawn wood

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the building sense behind the word, its compounds, and the beams it names.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从词中的「建筑物」古义、复合词与横梁义入手。

normal.en: Timber once meant a building, so the word still carries structure inside it.
normal.cn: timber 曾指建筑物，词里仍藏着「结构」。

normal.en: Timberyard and timber frame are the two compounds easiest to hold.
normal.cn: timberyard 与 timber frame 是最容易记住的两个复合词。

normal.en: Lumber is the American cousin; timber is the standing tree or the seasoned beam.
normal.cn: lumber 是美式近亲，timber 更偏向待伐的树或备好的梁。

normal.en: Good timber is a compliment, meaning a person worth building.
normal.cn: good timber 是褒义，指值得造就的人。

normal.en: The lumberjack shout Timber uses the word itself as the warning.
normal.cn: 伐木工的喊声 Timber 就是把词本身当作警告。

abstract.en: Picture a sawn face of pine with rings running in tight curves.
abstract.cn: 想象锯开的松木截面，年轮卷成紧密的圈。

abstract.en: Think of a roof held up by dark beams crossing the ceiling.
abstract.cn: 想一根根深色横梁在天花板上交错的屋顶。

abstract.en: A forest is a warehouse of timber standing on its own roots.
abstract.cn: 森林就是一座长在根上的木料仓库。

examples.en: The house uses timber from the nearby forest.
examples.cn: 这幢房子用的是附近森林的木材。

examples.en: Two roof timbers were replaced after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨后更换了两根屋顶横梁。

examples.en: The scouts learned to shout timber before a tree fell.
examples.cn: 童子军学会在树倒下前喊「倒树了」。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提木伯」——那位伯伯一提木头就懂，木料好坏一看便知。

root: 古英语 timber（建筑物）受古诺斯语 timberr（建筑、建材）影响，义转为「建筑用木材」，再引申为横梁、林木与「人的素质」。

sensesIntro.en: Starting from a built structure, the entry moves through the wood it is made of, the beams and mine props, the forest that supplies it, and the human qualities that building needs.
sensesIntro.cn: 本词从「建成的构造」出发，经过所用的木料、横梁与矿用支架、供材的森林，走到建造所需的人的素质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: squared beams stacked and waiting to become a structure.
core.cn: 核心意象：码放整齐的木方，等着被搭成构造。

branches.en: Prepared wood and the land that produces it.
branches.cn: 备好的木料与出产木料的土地。

branches.en: Trees regarded as a harvest.
Structural and supporting wood.
The beam as a metaphor for support.
Human quality and the warning shout.
branches.cn: 人的素质与倒树的警告喊声。

intro.en: The noun is native and takes the ordinary English endings for its adjective and noun forms, plus compounds with yard and frame.
intro.cn: 这是个本土名词，加常规英语词尾构成形容词与名词形式，并与 yard、frame 组成复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the Latin lines below list borrowed words for wood and for building that often pair with timber in technical texts.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；下面列出的拉丁词是技术文献中常与 timber 搭配的借词。

items.example: The whole meaning of the word rests on this noun.
items.exampleCN: 全词意义都落在这个名词上。

items.example: It reinforced the material sense in northern English.
items.exampleCN: 它在英格兰北方强化了「材料」义。

items.example: Timbered describes a frame house.
Timbering names the wooden supports of a shaft.
items.exampleCN: timbering 指矿井巷道的木支撑。

items.meaning: an enclosed place for work or storage
items.meaningCN: 用于作业或存放的场地
items.example: Timberyard is where boards are stacked.
Timbers can mean several beams.
Timber frame is a kind of construction.
items.exampleCN: timber frame 是一种结构方式。

items.meaning: a structure built of a material
items.example: Timberwork appears on old house fronts.
items.exampleCN: timberwork 出现在老房子的正立面上。

definition_zh: 时间；时候；次数；时代；时机；计时；为……定时
definition_en: the continuous passage in which events happen, a particular moment or occasion, or a period of history; also to measure or schedule how long something takes
core_image: 沙漏颈口的细沙一粒粒落下，谁也停不住
scene: 老街的钟表铺里挂满大小不一的旧钟。The old clocks in the shop kept different time, each off by a minute or two.
sceneCN: 这里 time 是「（钟表所指示的）时间」（第 1 个义项：时间、时刻）；句意为店里的旧钟各走各的时间，每只都差一两分钟。画面里有钟面、指针与柜台。

pos.zh: 名词：时间；时候；次数；时代
动词：为……计时；安排……的时间

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -ly 构成，义为「及时的」
加 -less 构成，义为「永恒的；超越时间的」
加 -ing 名词化，义为「时机把握；计时」
加 -er 构成，义为「计时器」

senses.title: The passage of time
senses.definition: the continuous progress of seconds, hours, and years in which events occur
senses.definitionCN: 事件在其中发生的秒、小时、年的连续流逝
senses.example: Time passes more slowly when you are waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 等待时时间过得格外慢。
senses.why: Old English tima named a limited or allotted period; extending it indefinitely gives the modern sense of time itself.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 tima 指一段有限、被分配的时间；把它无限延展便成了现代的「时间本身」。

senses.title: A particular moment
senses.definition: a specific point or moment at which something happens
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的具体时刻
senses.example: It is time to go home.
senses.exampleCN: 该回家了。
senses.why: A point inside the stream of time is itself a small allotted piece of it.
senses.whyCN: 时间之流中的一处，本身就是一小段被分配的时间。

senses.title: An occasion or instance
senses.definition: one occasion on which something happens, counted with a number
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的一次，与数词连用计数
senses.example: This is the third time she has called.
senses.exampleCN: 这是她第三次打电话来。
senses.why: Each separate span of time becomes a countable unit, so repetition is counted in times.
senses.whyCN: 每一段独立的时间成可数单位，重复便以 times 计数。

senses.title: A period of history
senses.definition: a stretch of years associated with a distinct way of life or a ruler
senses.definitionCN: 与某种生活方式或某位统治者相关的一段年代
senses.example: In Roman times the road carried soldiers and grain.
senses.exampleCN: 在罗马时代，这条路上运送着士兵与粮食。
senses.why: Large allotted spans of history are time on the grandest scale.
senses.whyCN: 历史上被划出的大段时间，是最大尺度的时间。

senses.title: A suitable moment
senses.definition: a moment favourable for a particular action
senses.definitionCN: 适合某种行动的时刻
senses.example: Now is the time to ask for help.
senses.exampleCN: 现在是求助的时机。
senses.why: If time is allotted, some of it is given for a purpose, and that purpose opens a window.
senses.whyCN: 如果时间是分配的，其中总有一段给了某个目的，那段就是窗口。

senses.title: To measure how long something takes
senses.definition: to measure or record the duration of an activity
senses.definitionCN: 测量或记录某项活动的时长
senses.example: The coach timed every runner with a stopwatch.
senses.exampleCN: 教练用秒表给每位跑者计时。
senses.why: Telling time turns the noun into the act of counting the passing units.
senses.whyCN: 读取时间把名词变成了数过单位的行为。

senses.title: To schedule at a moment
senses.definition: to arrange for something to happen at a planned moment
senses.definitionCN: 安排某事在计划好的时刻发生
senses.example: They timed the launch for early morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把发布会定在清早。
senses.why: To give a portion of time to an event is to decide its allotted moment.
senses.whyCN: 把一段时间分给某个事件，就是决定它被分配的时刻。

senses.title: Times of rhythm or music
senses.definition: the rhythm or speed of a piece of music, or the beat of an activity
senses.definitionCN: 乐曲的节奏或速度，也指活动的节拍
senses.example: The drummer set the time for the whole band.
senses.exampleCN: 鼓手为整个乐队定下节拍。
senses.why: Music measures time in equal beats, so the word names the very beat it counts.
senses.whyCN: 音乐以等分的拍计量时间，于是本词也被赋予它所数的那一拍。

senses.title: Times as multiplication
senses.definition: used after a number to show repeated quantity in multiplication
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字后表示乘法中的倍数
senses.example: Four times five is twenty.
senses.exampleCN: 四乘五等于二十。
senses.why: When a span repeats a number of times, counting it multiplies; hence the arithmetic sense.
senses.whyCN: 当一段时间重复若干次，计数就变成相乘，于是有了算术义。

senses.title: Time on a clock
senses.definition: the reading shown by a clock or watch
senses.definitionCN: 钟表显示的读数
senses.example: The clocks in the shop kept different time.
senses.exampleCN: 店里的钟各走各的时间。
senses.why: A clock exists to convert the invisible stream into a number we can read.
senses.whyCN: 钟表的存在就是把看不见的流动变成可读的数字。

intro.en: The English noun is native, related to words in other Germanic languages for a time or hour, and its root sense is an allotted or divided period.
intro.cn: 这个英语名词是本土词，与其它日耳曼语中表示「时间、时辰」的词同源，其根本义是「被分配、被划分的一段时间」。

items.en: Tima meant a limited period or a measured hour.
items.cn: tima 意为有限的时段或量定的时辰。

items.en: Cognates in Old Norse and Old High German also mean time or hour, pointing to a shared root.
items.cn: 古诺斯语与古高地德语中的同源词同样表示时间、时辰，指向共同词根。

items.en: The noun expands from a limited span to time in general and to counted occasions.
items.cn: 名词从有限时段扩展到一般意义的时间，以及可数的事件次数。

items.en: The verb to time, meaning to measure or schedule, is formed from the noun.
items.cn: 表示计时或安排时间的动词 time 由名词构成。

items.en: Clock and railway keeping time fix the phrase as a standard of accuracy.
items.cn: 钟表与铁路的「对时间」让这一短语成为准确性的标准。

items.en: The sense of dating from a clock, and of rhythm in music, settle as ordinary uses.
items.cn: 钟表读数义与音乐节拍义都落定为日常用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word family built on time, and the near-meaning group lists other words for periods and for timing.
note.cn: 形近组收集以 time 为词干构成的词族，近义组列出表示时段与计时的其他词。

entries.definition: happening at just the right moment
not affected by the passing of time
a device that measures intervals of time
a herb used in cooking, a different word
entries.definitionCN: 百里香；只是读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a length of time with a stated character
a long period named by its events
a very short point in time
the length of time something lasts

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the allotted-period idea, from its fixed phrases, and from the family it produced.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「被分配的时段」这一观念、固定短语与派生词族入手。

normal.en: On time and in time differ: on time is punctual, in time is early enough.
normal.cn: on time 是准时，in time 是还来得及，两者不同。

normal.en: Take your time literally means take a portion of time for yourself.
normal.cn: take your time 字面就是为自己取一段时间。

normal.en: The times of counting three times and the times of multiplying share one span repeated.
normal.cn: 三次的 times 与乘法的 times 都是同一段的重复。

normal.en: Timely, timeless, timer all grow from time with ordinary endings.
normal.cn: timely、timeless、timer 都由 time 加常规词尾构成。

normal.en: The thyme herb sounds the same but has a Greek plant name.
normal.cn: 香草 thyme 读音相同，但名字来自希腊的植物名。

abstract.en: Picture sand running without pause through the neck of a glass.
abstract.cn: 想象细沙不停从玻璃瓶颈落下。

abstract.en: Think of a clock face where hands never agree, just as in the old shop.
abstract.cn: 想一面指针永不统一的钟面，正如那家旧钟铺。

abstract.en: A meeting is a small box drawn round a piece of the day.
abstract.cn: 一场会面就是在一天里画出的小方框。

examples.en: We have enough time to walk to the station.
examples.cn: 我们有足够时间走到车站。

examples.en: The race was timed with an electronic system.
examples.cn: 比赛用电子系统计时。

examples.en: He has told the same story many times.
examples.cn: 同一个故事他讲过很多次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太」——太久了，沙子漏完，时间也没了。

root: 古英语 tima（时段、时辰），日耳曼语族固有词，与古诺斯语、古高地德语中的同源词同义，词根义为「被划分、被分配的时间」。

sensesIntro.en: The allotted span widens into time itself, narrows into a moment, is counted as an occasion, is stretched into an era, and is measured by clocks, music, and arithmetic.
sensesIntro.cn: 被分配的时段放宽成时间本身，收窄成一个时刻，被数成次数，被拉长为时代，也被钟表、音乐与算术计量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sand falling at an even rate through a narrow neck.
core.cn: 核心意象：细沙以均匀速度从窄颈落下。

branches.en: The flow itself, unlimited.
A point or window singled out of the flow.
branches.cn: 从流中挑出的点或窗口。

branches.en: The span counted and repeated.
Long spans and rhythmic beats.
branches.cn: 长的时代与有节拍的拍子。

branches.en: The measurement and scheduling of time.

intro.en: The native noun takes a set of ordinary English endings and compounds, which is the main affix story here.
intro.cn: 这个本土名词接一串常规英语词尾与复合成分，这就是这里的构词主线。

latinIntro.en: Time has no Latin etymon; the borrowed Latin items below are ordinary companions in technical writing about time.
latinIntro.cn: time 没有拉丁词源；下面的拉丁词是时间类技术写作中常见的借词。

items.example: The root sense survives in the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 整个词族都保留这一词根义。

items.example: Timely means at the right time.
Timeless means without time.
Timing is the skill of choosing the moment.
items.exampleCN: timing 指把握时机的技巧。

items.example: A timer measures intervals.
A timetable arranges a school day.
Times serves as plural and verb form.
items.exampleCN: times 既是复数也是动词形式。

items.meaning: working only part of the week
items.example: Part-time work leaves hours free.
items.exampleCN: part-time 的工作会空出若干小时。

definition_zh: 时间表；时刻表；课程表；日程表；制定时间表
definition_en: a list or chart showing the times at which classes, trains, or events take place, or the plan itself
core_image: 一张方格纸，每一格都填着一个钟点与一件事
scene: 新学期的教室后墙贴出了一张表，密密麻麻写满课程。Someone had already written the timetable on the blackboard for the first week.
sceneCN: 这里 timetable 是「课程表」（第 3 个义项：学校的上课时间表）；句意为有人已经把第一周的时间表写在黑板上。画面里有方格表格、钟点与粉笔字。

pos.zh: 名词：时间表；时刻表；课程表
动词：为……安排时间；列入时间表

derivatives.zh: 由词根 time 加过去分词结尾，义为「定时的；计时的」
由词根 time 加 -er 构成，义为「计时器」
由词根 time 加 -ing 构成，义为「时机；计时」

senses.title: A list of times
senses.definition: a list showing the times at which things are planned to happen
senses.definitionCN: 列出各项事情计划发生时间的清单
senses.example: The new timetable cuts ten minutes off the morning train.
senses.exampleCN: 新时刻表让早班列车少花十分钟。
senses.why: A table in English is both a chart and a flat surface, so a table of times is a timetable.
senses.whyCN: 英语的 table 既指表格又指平面，所以「时间的表」就是 timetable。

senses.title: A schedule for transport
senses.definition: a printed or posted list of train, bus, or plane times
senses.definitionCN: 张贴或印刷的班次时间表
senses.example: Check the bus timetable before you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前查一下公交时刻表。
senses.why: Transport is the place where exact times matter most, so this is the sense most people meet first.
senses.whyCN: 交通是最讲究精确时间的场合，因此这是多数人最先遇到的用法。

senses.title: A school class schedule
senses.definition: a weekly chart of lessons showing subject, teacher, and room
senses.definitionCN: 标明科目、教师与教室的一周课表
senses.example: Our timetable is full every afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们每天下午的课表都排满了。
senses.why: School life is divided into fixed slots just like a printed table.
senses.whyCN: 学校生活被划成固定格子，正如印出来的表格。

senses.title: A plan of events
senses.definition: a plan listing the order and dates of a series of events or steps
senses.definitionCN: 列出系列活动或步骤顺序与日期的计划
senses.example: The committee agreed on a timetable for the reforms.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会就改革的日程表达成了一致。
senses.why: Beyond clocks and classes, any long plan can be laid out as a table of dates.
senses.whyCN: 除钟点和课程之外，任何长期计划都可摊成一张日期表。

senses.title: To schedule something
senses.definition: to arrange for an event or service to take place at a stated time
senses.definitionCN: 安排某活动或服务在特定时间进行
senses.example: The hearing is timetabled for next Tuesday.
senses.exampleCN: 听证会安排在周二。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: to put an item into one of the table's slots.
senses.whyCN: 名词变动词：把一件事放进表格的某一格。

senses.title: A political programme of dates
senses.definition: a published plan of dates for proposed legislation or negotiations
senses.definitionCN: 公布的法案或谈判的时间规划
senses.example: The government published a timetable for the withdrawal.
senses.exampleCN: 政府公布了撤军时间规划。
senses.why: Public promises need dates, so the word entered politics as a schedule of commitments.
senses.whyCN: 公开承诺需要日期，本词因此以「承诺日程」的身份进入政治。

senses.title: A posted chart in a station
senses.definition: the large board on a platform that shows departure times
senses.definitionCN: 站台上显示发车时间的大牌
senses.example: A crowd stared at the timetable after the delay was announced.
senses.exampleCN: 延误公布后，一群人盯着时刻牌看。
senses.why: The document becomes a fixed public object on a wall, readable by anyone waiting.
senses.whyCN: 文件成了墙上固定的公共物件，任何等待的人都能读。

senses.title: A method of learning in small steps
senses.definition: a scheme that sets out the order in which material is learned
senses.definitionCN: 规定学习材料先后顺序的方案
senses.example: Some language courses sell a ready-made timetable of lessons.
senses.exampleCN: 有些语言课程出售现成的分步教学计划。
senses.why: Teaching is a sequence of steps, and a sequence laid out in order is again a table.
senses.whyCN: 教学是一串步骤，按序排开的步骤又是一张表。

intro.en: The word is a straightforward English compound of time and table, put together in the modern period when printed schedules became common.
intro.cn: 这是一个由 time 与 table 直接组成的英语复合词，在印刷时刻表普及的近代成形。

items.en: Tima supplied the first element, meaning an allotted period.
items.cn: 第一成分 tima 意为被分配的时段。

items.en: Tabula, a board or writing tablet, is the distant source of table.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tabula（板、书写用的平板）是 table 的远源。

items.en: Tabule entered English in the sense of a flat writing surface.
items.cn: tabule 以「平面书写板」的意义进入英语。

items.en: Table extends from a flat board to any arranged set of figures or times.
items.cn: table 从平板扩展到任何排好的数字或时间列。

items.en: Timetable appears as printed railway schedules spread in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 随着十九世纪铁路时刻表普及，timetable 出现。

items.en: The word spreads from transport to schools, projects, and political plans.
items.cn: 本词从交通扩展到学校、项目与政治的规划。

note.en: The look-alike group collects time compounds, and the near-meaning group gathers the words for schedules and plans.
note.cn: 形近组收集以 time 开头的复合词，近义组聚集表示时刻表与计划的词。

entries.definition: a person or device that records time
the work of arranging a schedule
listed in a schedule
a class slot fixed in the school schedule
a plan listing times for tasks or travel
a list of items to be discussed at a meeting
a planned series of events
a list showing who works when

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the two halves of the compound and from the places the word appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从复合词的两半以及本词出现的地方入手。

normal.en: Timetable is simply time plus table, a table filled with times.
normal.cn: timetable 就是 time 加 table，填着时间的表。

normal.en: The railway gave the word its first home, so the train timetable came before the school one.
normal.cn: 铁路是本词最早的家，火车时刻表先于学校课表。

normal.en: The verb keeps the same spelling, so timetabled means put into a slot.
normal.cn: 动词拼写不变，timetabled 意为「已排定」。

normal.en: Draw up a timetable is the common verb phrase for making one.
normal.cn: draw up a timetable 是制造时间表的常用搭配。

normal.en: Agenda, roster, and schedule are its close cousins in the planning family.
normal.cn: agenda、roster、schedule 是计划类词里的近亲。

abstract.en: Picture a grid where every square holds a number and a name.
abstract.cn: 想象一张方格纸，每格都填着一个号码与一个名字。

abstract.en: Think of a platform board clicking over to a new time.
abstract.cn: 想站台上的翻牌牌面咔哒一声跳到新时间。

abstract.en: A timetable is a promise made of hours.
abstract.cn: 时间表就是用小时写成的承诺。

examples.en: The new timetable starts on Monday.
examples.cn: 新时间表从周一开始。

examples.en: She checked the train timetable before booking a ticket.
examples.cn: 订票前她查了列车时刻表。

examples.en: The manager timetabled the training for Thursday afternoon.
examples.cn: 经理把培训安排在周四下午。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太木台布」——一块太木的台布，上面印着所有钟点。

root: 由 time（古英语 tima，时段）与 table（拉丁 tabula，板、书写平板）复合而成，十九世纪铁路印刷时刻表普及后定名。

sensesIntro.en: A table of hours covers trains, lessons, projects, and political promises, and the verb then puts anything into one of its slots.
sensesIntro.cn: 一张小时表既覆盖列车，也覆盖课程、项目与政治承诺；动词则把任何事放进表格的某一格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grid in which each cell holds a clock time and a task.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张方格表，每格一个钟点与一件事。

branches.en: The printed list and its posted form.
branches.cn: 印刷清单及其张贴形态。

branches.en: Transport as the word's first home.
Schools and step-by-step teaching.
Long plans and political dates.
The verb of placing something in a slot.
branches.cn: 把某事放进格子的动词用法。

intro.en: This compound is built from two free English words, so the affix work looks at its halves and the endings that make it a verb.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由两个独立英语词构成，因此构词要点在于它的两半以及把它变成动词的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Only the second half reaches back to Latin tabula; the Latin list gives that word and near neighbours.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后半可追溯到拉丁语 tabula；拉丁表给出该词及邻近的对照词。

items.example: The first half names what the chart lists.
items.exampleCN: 前半标明表格所记述的东西。

items.example: The second half names the form.
This is the remote source of table.
Timetables serves as plural and verb form.
items.exampleCN: timetables 既是复数也是动词形式。

items.example: Timetabled means placed in a slot.
Timetabling is the work of scheduling.
An under-timetabled class wastes hours.
A re-timetableable slot can still be moved.

definition_zh: 锡；罐头；金属罐；镀锡铁皮；装罐
definition_en: a soft silver-white metal that does not rust easily; also a metal container for food, and the metal sheet itself
core_image: 一只银亮的小罐，表面泛着柔和的白光，敲一下有闷响
scene: 厨房架子上码着一排贴着标签的小罐，标签都朝外。She opened a tin of tomatoes for the soup.
sceneCN: 这里 tin 是「罐头」（第 2 个义项：装食物的金属罐）；句意是她为做汤开了一罐番茄。画面里有铁架、标签与银色罐头。

pos.zh: 名词：锡；罐头；金属罐；铁皮
动词：把……装罐；镀锡

derivatives.zh: 加过去分词结尾，义为「罐装的」
加 -y 构成，义为「有锡味的；声音尖细的」
复合词，义为「锡箔」

senses.title: The metal tin
senses.definition: a soft, silver-white metal used in alloys and in coating steel
senses.definitionCN: 一种柔软银白色的金属，用于合金及镀钢
senses.example: Bronze is mostly copper with some tin added.
senses.exampleCN: 青铜主要是铜，加入了一些锡。
senses.why: Old English tin named the metal, borrowed from a Germanic word whose further origin is uncertain.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 tin 指这种金属，借自日耳曼语词，更远的来源不确定。

senses.title: A food container
senses.definition: a sealed metal container in which food is preserved
senses.definitionCN: 密封装食品的金属容器
senses.example: She opened a tin of tomatoes for the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她开了一罐番茄做汤。
senses.why: Because the coating was tin, the can itself took the metal's name.
senses.whyCN: 由于镀层是锡，罐子本身便借了金属的名字。

senses.title: The metal sheet
senses.definition: thin steel sheet coated with tin for making cans and pans
senses.definitionCN: 用于制罐、制锅的镀锡薄钢板
senses.example: The roof was patched with a sheet of tin.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶用一块铁皮补过。
senses.why: A can is thin metal plus a tin coating, so the sheet is called tin as well.
senses.whyCN: 罐头是薄金属加锡层，所以那张薄板也叫 tin。

senses.title: Any metal container
senses.definition: a metal container of other shapes, such as a biscuit tin
senses.definitionCN: 其它形状的金属容器，如饼干盒
senses.example: The biscuit tin was empty by Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 到周日饼干盒就空了。
senses.why: Once the can took the name, any metal box followed in British usage.
senses.whyCN: 既然罐头先借了这名，英式用法中各种金属盒也跟上。

senses.title: To preserve in a can
senses.definition: to preserve food by sealing it in a metal container
senses.definitionCN: 把食物密封在金属容器里保存
senses.example: The factory tins the fruit within hours of picking.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂在水果采摘后几小时内完成罐装。
senses.why: The verb is the can turned into an action: putting food into the named object.
senses.whyCN: 动词把罐头变成动作：把食物放进那个已命名的物体。

senses.title: To coat with tin
senses.definition: to cover a surface with a thin layer of tin or solder
senses.definitionCN: 在表面覆上一层锡或焊料
senses.example: The worker tinned the ends of the wires before joining.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在接线前先给导线端头镀锡。
senses.why: The metal returns as a verb: applying the substance to another thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个金属又回到动词：把它施到别的东西上。

senses.title: A baking mould
senses.definition: a shallow metal mould used for baking
senses.definitionCN: 用于烘焙的浅金属模具
senses.example: Pour the batter into the greased tin.
senses.exampleCN: 把面糊倒进抹了油的烤模。
senses.why: A mould is a metal container for dough, so the container sense extends to kitchen shapes.
senses.whyCN: 烤模是装面团的金属容器，容器义便扩展到厨房器形。

senses.title: Slang for money
senses.definition: money, used in informal British speech
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中表示钱
senses.example: He counted out the tin for the taxi.
senses.exampleCN: 他把打车钱数了出来。
senses.why: Metal coins and small cash echo the silver metal, though the slang link is not certain.
senses.whyCN: 金属硬币与零钱让人联想到这种银色金属，但这一俚语关联不确定。

intro.en: The metal name is Germanic in origin, and the container sense grew out of the tin coating that once protected iron cans.
intro.cn: 金属名来自日耳曼语，容器义则源自当年保护铁罐的锡镀层。

items.en: Tin is recorded early as the name of the metal.
items.cn: tin 早期即有记载，指这种金属。

items.en: Related forms in other Germanic languages name the same metal, pointing to a common root.
items.cn: 其它日耳曼语中的相关形式指同一金属，指向共同词根。

items.en: The pre-Germanic source is debated and may be an early borrowing from a Mediterranean language.
items.cn: 日耳曼语之前的来源尚有争论，可能是早期从地中海某语输入的借词。

items.en: Tinned iron plates for cans give the container the name tin.
items.cn: 用于制罐的镀锡铁皮让容器得名 tin。

items.en: British usage extends tin to biscuit boxes and baking moulds.
items.cn: 英式用法把 tin 扩展到饼干盒与烤模。

items.en: The verb tins food and also tins wire, from the same metal.
items.cn: 动词用法既指罐装食品，也指给导线镀锡，都源于这种金属。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the metal's family and near spellings, and the near-meaning group lists metals and containers.
note.cn: 形近组收集这种金属的词族与相近拼写，近义组列出金属与容器类词。

entries.definition: preserved in a can, or coated with tin
tasting or sounding of tin
very thin metal sheet used to wrap food
a slight shade of colour, a different word
entries.definitionCN: 色调；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a sealed metal container for food, the American word
a metal made by mixing two or more metals
a metal used to join other metal parts
anything used to hold something

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the metal, its coating, and the containers the coating named.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从金属本身、镀层以及由镀层得名的容器入手。

normal.en: Tin is the metal, can is the object; British tin and American can name the same thing.
normal.cn: 锡是金属，can 是器物；英式 tin 与美式 can 指同一物。

normal.en: Tinned means both canned food and coated wire, because the metal does both jobs.
normal.cn: tinned 既是罐装食品也是镀锡导线，因为锡兼任两职。

normal.en: Tin foil begins as tin and is now usually aluminium, but the name holds.
normal.cn: 锡箔起初真用锡，现在多用铝，名字却留住了。

normal.en: A biscuit tin and a baking tin show how far the container sense reaches.
normal.cn: 饼干罐与烤模显示了容器义延伸得多远。

normal.en: Tin is soft, so it coats stronger steel instead of being used alone.
normal.cn: 锡很软，因此常用来镀在更硬的钢上，而不是单独使用。

abstract.en: Picture a silver ribbon of metal bent easily round a finger.
abstract.cn: 想象一条银色金属带，轻易就能绕在手指上。

abstract.en: Think of a row of tins on a shelf with their labels turned out.
abstract.cn: 想架子上一排标签朝外的罐头。

abstract.en: A tin can keeps a summer's fruit alive into winter.
abstract.cn: 一只罐头把夏天的水果留到冬天。

examples.en: Bronze is made of copper and tin.
examples.cn: 青铜由铜与锡制成。

examples.en: He bought a tin of sardines for the journey.
examples.cn: 他为旅途买了一罐沙丁鱼。

examples.en: The peaches were tinned the same day they were picked.
examples.cn: 桃子采摘当天就被装成了罐头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「停」——一罐头的食物停了很久也不坏。

root: 古英语 tin（锡），源自日耳曼语共同词；更远的来源不确定。十九世纪镀锡铁罐普及后，容器义由镀层得名。

sensesIntro.en: The metal gives the name, the coated steel gives the can, and from the can the word spreads to boxes, moulds, canning, and even money.
sensesIntro.cn: 金属给出名字，镀层给出罐头，而由罐头一词又扩展到盒子、烤模、罐装乃至钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft silver metal shining along the surface of a can.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层柔和银光贴在罐子的表面。

branches.en: The metal as substance.
The coated plate and the containers made from it.
branches.cn: 镀层铁皮及其制成的容器。

branches.en: Putting the substance or the food where it belongs.
branches.cn: 把物质或食物放进它该在的地方。

branches.en: Kitchen shapes of the same idea.
The slang turn to money.

intro.en: The word is short and Germanic, so its endings are the everyday English ones that build its adjective, noun, and verb forms.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且属日耳曼语，其词尾都是构成形容词、名词与动词的常规英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Tin has no Latin etymon; the Latin items below are borrowed words for metal that often appear beside it.
latinIntro.cn: tin 没有拉丁词源；下面的拉丁词是与金属相关的借词。

items.example: The short root carries the whole substance.
items.exampleCN: 这个短词根承载整个物质义。

items.example: Tinned food is sealed in cans.
Tinny describes a thin metallic sound.
items.exampleCN: tinny 形容细薄的金属声。

items.example: Tinning is the work of coating with tin.
Tins is both a plural and a verb form.
items.exampleCN: tins 既是复数也是动词形式。

items.example: Tinfoil is a thin metal sheet.
A tin opener cuts the lid.
items.exampleCN: tin opener 用来割开罐盖。

items.meaning: a place where metal is dug
items.example: A tin mine produces the ore.

definition_zh: 极小的；微小的；细小的；微不足道的
definition_en: extremely small in size, amount, or importance
core_image: 掌心上一粒几乎看不见的小沙，得眯起眼才分得清
scene: 雨后的石阶上，一只小生物正慢慢横着爬。A tiny crab crossed the wet step and disappeared into a crack.
sceneCN: 这里 tiny 是「极小的」（第 1 个义项：体积非常小）；句意为一只极小的蟹爬过湿石阶，钻进石缝不见了。画面有水光、石阶与一条细缝。

pos.zh: 形容词：极小的；微小的；细小的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ness 构成，义为「微小；极小」
形容词比较级，义为「更小的」
形容词最高级，义为「最小的」

senses.title: Extremely small in size
senses.definition: very small indeed in physical size
senses.definitionCN: 体积确实非常小
senses.example: A tiny insect landed on the page.
senses.exampleCN: 一只极小的虫子落在书页上。
senses.why: The word is probably a northern form related to little, with the ending shaping a diminutive.
senses.whyCN: 本词很可能是与 little 相关的北方方言形式，词尾带有「小」的意味。

senses.title: Small in amount
senses.definition: very small in quantity or degree
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度上非常小
senses.example: Only a tiny amount of salt is needed.
senses.exampleCN: 只需要极少一点盐。
senses.why: The size sense transfers to quantity: a small amount is measured on the same scale as a small object.
senses.whyCN: 大小义转到数量上：少量与小的物体用同一把尺子衡量。

senses.title: Small and endearing
senses.definition: small in a way that makes people fond
senses.definitionCN: 小得让人心生喜爱
senses.example: She bought a tiny pair of boots for the doll.
senses.exampleCN: 她给娃娃买了一双小小的靴子。
senses.why: Smallness plus care gives the affectionate tone the word often carries.
senses.whyCN: 细小的体积配上用心，本词常带着亲昵的口气。

senses.title: Small in importance
senses.definition: of very little importance or significance
senses.definitionCN: 重要性或意义很小
senses.example: The differences between the two drafts were tiny.
senses.exampleCN: 两份草稿之间的差别微乎其微。
senses.why: If physical size is near zero, importance measured the same way is also near zero.
senses.whyCN: 若体积近乎零，用同一把尺子衡量的重要性也近乎零。

senses.title: A tiny fraction
senses.definition: a very small proportion of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 整体中一个非常小的份额
senses.example: A tiny fraction of the budget went to repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 预算中极小一部分用于维修。
senses.why: A part cut small enough is described with the size word rather than a counting word.
senses.whyCN: 被切得足够小的一份，用大小词而非计数词来描述。

senses.title: The tiniest detail
senses.definition: the most minute element, in the superlative tiniest
senses.definitionCN: 最高级形式下指最细小的要素
senses.example: She noticed the tiniest change in his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她发觉他声音里最细微的变化。
senses.why: Even a detail has a size, and at the smallest scale it becomes tiny.
senses.whyCN: 细节也有大小，到了最小尺度就成了 tiny。

senses.title: Small and young
senses.definition: used of a very young person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 形容年幼的人或动物
senses.example: The tiny kitten could not yet open its eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 那只幼小的猫还睁不开眼。
senses.why: Young bodies are small bodies, so age and size share the same word.
senses.whyCN: 幼小的身体就是小小的身体，年龄与大小共用一词。

senses.title: Small in comparison
senses.definition: small when set beside something much larger
senses.definitionCN: 与更大之物相比显得很小
senses.example: From the air the ship looked tiny.
senses.exampleCN: 从空中看去那艘船显得极小。
senses.why: The word often measures against a larger frame, making size relative rather than fixed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常相对更大的参照来衡量，因此大小是相对的。

intro.en: The adjective appears in the late sixteenth century, probably from a northern or British dialect form related to little, with a diminutive ending.
intro.cn: 这个形容词在十六世纪末出现，很可能来自与 little 相关的地方方言形式，并带有表小的词尾。

items.en: A dialect form tine or tiney is recorded for little or small.
items.cn: 方言形式 tine、tiney 已有记载，意为「小的」。

items.en: Scholars connect it with little, but the exact path is not settled.
items.cn: 学者把它与 little 联系起来，但确切路径尚未定论。

items.en: Tiny is recorded in written English from the late sixteenth century.
items.cn: tiny 自十六世纪末见于书面英语。

items.en: The comparative tinier and the superlative tiniest stabilize by the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 比较级 tinier 与最高级 tiniest 在十八世纪定型。

items.en: The word becomes the everyday strong form of small, warmer than minute.
items.cn: 本词成为 small 的日常强形式，比 minute 更带感情。

items.en: It spreads from physical size to amount, detail, and importance.
items.cn: 它从体积扩展到数量、细节与重要性。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other words ending in a similar shape, while the near-meaning group gathers the scale of smallness.
note.cn: 形近组列出结尾形状相似的其他词，近义组则聚集「小」的程度上的一组词。

entries.definition: the quality of being extremely small
the most extremely small
a soft metal, a different word
a light ringing sound, a different word
entries.definitionCN: 叮当声；只是形近，词源不同

entries.definition: extremely small, in a formal register
made as a much smaller copy
small in degree or amount
extremely large

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the word's dialect origins, its scale, and the comparisons it invites.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从它的方言来源、尺度以及它引出的对比入手。

normal.en: Tiny is probably a dialect cousin of little, so the small meaning is built in.
normal.cn: tiny 很可能是 little 的方言近亲，小的意思天生带着。

normal.en: Tinier and tiniest follow the y to i rule: y becomes i before -er.
normal.cn: tinier 与 tiniest 遵守 y 变 i 的规则。

normal.en: A tiny bit is the everyday phrase for a very small quantity.
normal.cn: a tiny bit 是表示极少量的日常说法。

normal.en: The tiniest detail uses the superlative for the finest point.
normal.cn: the tiniest detail 用最高级表示最细微之处。

normal.en: Minute is formal, tiny is warm; huge is the exact opposite.
normal.cn: minute 偏正式，tiny 更亲切，huge 正好相反。

abstract.en: Picture a pinhead with a whole insect balanced on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根针的针头上落着一整只虫子。

abstract.en: Think of a ship seen from a plane window, no bigger than a speck.
abstract.cn: 想从机窗望见的一艘船，小得像一粒斑点。

abstract.en: A tiny thing demands that you lean closer, and leaning is the word's feeling.
abstract.cn: 微小之物逼你凑近，凑近正是这个词的感觉。

examples.en: A tiny bird was perched on the wire.
examples.cn: 一只极小的鸟停在电线上。

examples.en: Add a tiny bit of sugar to the sauce.
examples.cn: 在酱汁里加一点点糖。

examples.en: From the top of the hill the houses looked tiny.
examples.cn: 从山顶看去，那些房子显得很小。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太迷你」——太迷你了，小得放在掌心都找不着。

root: 一般认为与 little 相关的方言形式 tiney 有关，词尾带表小色彩，确切来源不确定；十六世纪末进入书面英语。

sensesIntro.en: One scale of smallness runs through the entry: physical size first, then amount, affection, importance, fractions, details, young creatures, and size seen from far away.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条「小」的尺度贯穿全词：先体积，再到数量、亲昵、重要性、比例、细节、幼小以及远观的大小。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speck on the palm that you must squint to see.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心一粒得眯眼才看得见的尘点。

branches.en: Small bodies, including young ones.
branches.cn: 小的身体，包括幼小的个体。

branches.en: Smallness measured in quantity and proportion.
branches.cn: 以数量与比例衡量的小。

branches.en: The affectionate colour of the size.
Smallness of importance and of detail.
branches.cn: 重要性与细节上的微小。

branches.en: Small compared with a larger frame.
branches.cn: 与更大参照相比显出的小。

intro.en: The adjective takes the regular English endings for comparison and a noun, plus the y to i spelling change.
intro.cn: 这个形容词接常规英语的比较级与名词词尾，并遵守 y 变 i 的拼写规则。

latinIntro.en: Tiny has no Latin etymon; the Latin items below offer the formal scale of smallness for comparison.
latinIntro.cn: tiny 没有拉丁词源；下面的拉丁词提供正式语体的「小」尺度作对照。

items.example: The ending gives tiny its adjective shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾让 tiny 成为形容词。

items.example: Tinier means even smaller.
Tiniest means the smallest.
Tininess names the quality.

items.meaning: y becomes i before a suffix
items.meaningCN: 后缀前 y 变 i
items.example: Tiniest drops the y for i.
items.exampleCN: tiniest 把 y 换成 i。

items.example: Tinish is not standard but would mean somewhat small.
items.exampleCN: tinish 不属标准词，但意为「有点小」。

items.example: Tiny has no common -ly adverb.
items.exampleCN: tiny 没有常用副词形式。

items.example: Semi-tiny is only a playful formation.

definition_zh: 尖端；顶端；小费；提示；诀窍；倾斜；倒出；给小费
definition_en: the pointed end of something; a small sum given for service, a useful piece of advice, or a dump site; also to lean over, or to give a gratuity
core_image: 一支笔的最末端，尖得能扎进纸里
scene: 服务员把账单放在桌上，客人多留了几张纸币。He left a generous tip on the tray and thanked the waiter.
sceneCN: 这里 tip 是「小费」（第 3 个义项：给服务者的小额赏钱）；句意为他在托盘上留下慷慨的小费并谢过服务员。画面有账单、托盘与纸币。

pos.zh: 名词：尖端；小费；提示；垃圾场
动词：倾斜；倒出；给小费；使倾斜

collocations.phrase: on the tip of one's tongue

derivatives.zh: 加 -er 构成，义为「给小费的人」或「翻斗车」
加 -ing 名词化，义为「给小费；倾倒」
复合词，义为「密报；通风报信」

senses.title: The pointed end
senses.definition: the narrow or pointed end of an object
senses.definitionCN: 物体细窄或尖锐的末端
senses.example: The tip of the pencil broke during the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试时铅笔尖断了。
senses.why: The word is probably a Scandinavian borrowing meaning the point or end of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 本词大概是斯堪的纳维亚语借词，意为物体的「尖、端」。

senses.title: The top of something
senses.definition: the highest or outermost part of something standing
senses.definitionCN: 直立之物最高或最外的一端
senses.example: Snow covered the tips of the pines.
senses.exampleCN: 积雪盖住了松树的树梢。
senses.why: A point is also the far end seen from the body, and for upright things that end is the top.
senses.whyCN: 尖端也是从主体看去的远端，对直立之物就是顶。

senses.title: Money for service
senses.definition: a small amount of money given to a waiter or other worker for good service
senses.definitionCN: 因服务好而给服务员等人的小额钱款
senses.example: He left a generous tip on the tray.
senses.exampleCN: 他在托盘上留了慷慨的小费。
senses.why: The gratuity sense has a separate and uncertain origin, probably from the idea of a small extra gift.
senses.whyCN: 小费义的来源另有一条、且不确定，大约有「小额额外馈赠」的意思。

senses.title: A piece of advice
senses.definition: a useful hint or piece of practical advice
senses.definitionCN: 有用的暗示或实用建议
senses.example: The guide ends with tips for travelling cheaply.
senses.exampleCN: 指南末尾给出了省钱旅行的建议。
senses.why: A hint points you toward the answer as the tip of an arrow points toward the target.
senses.whyCN: 提示像箭头一样指向答案。

senses.title: To lean or overturn
senses.definition: to lean to one side, or to make something fall over
senses.definitionCN: 向一侧倾斜，或使某物翻倒
senses.example: The table tipped when the heavy box landed on it.
senses.exampleCN: 重箱子砸下时桌子歪了。
senses.why: The verb probably comes from the same root, naming the motion that ends on one point.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词大概同源，命名只在一点着地的动作。

senses.title: To empty by tilting
senses.definition: to pour something out by tilting a container
senses.definitionCN: 把容器倾斜以倒出某物
senses.example: She tipped the rice into the bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 她把米倒进碗里。
senses.why: To tip a container is to lean it until its contents leave the point.
senses.whyCN: 使容器倾斜到内容物从尖端流出，就是倒。

senses.title: A place for waste
senses.definition: a place where rubbish is dumped, especially in British use
senses.definitionCN: 尤英式用法中倾倒垃圾的场地
senses.example: The old quarry became a rubbish tip.
senses.exampleCN: 老采石场变成了垃圾场。
senses.why: A tip is where material is emptied out, so the place of emptying takes the verb's name.
senses.whyCN: tip 是倒东西的地方，于是倾倒之处也得了动词的名字。

senses.title: To give a gratuity
senses.definition: to give a small sum of money to a waiter or other worker for service
senses.definitionCN: 因服务给服务员等人小额钱款
senses.example: They tipped the driver for carrying the bags.
senses.exampleCN: 他们因司机帮忙搬包而给了小费。
senses.why: The noun of the gratuity becomes an action, as with most such money words.
senses.whyCN: 与多数钱款类名词一样，小费名词也变成了动作。

senses.title: A piece of insider news
senses.definition: a private warning or piece of information about a race or a plan
senses.definitionCN: 关于比赛或计划的私下警告或消息
senses.example: A tip about the horse's injury changed the betting.
senses.exampleCN: 关于那匹马受伤的消息改变了押注。
senses.why: News given on the side also points the receiver in the right direction.
senses.whyCN: 私下递送的消息同样把人指向正确方向。

senses.title: The tip of the iceberg
senses.definition: used in the phrase the tip of the iceberg for a small visible part of a large hidden problem
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 the tip of the iceberg，指巨大隐情中可见的一小部分
senses.example: The missing files were only the tip of the iceberg.
senses.exampleCN: 丢失的文件只是冰山一角。
senses.why: Only the pointed tip shows above the surface, so the visible part is the word for the end of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 只有尖端露在水面上，可见的部分正是「末端」一词。

intro.en: At least two histories meet in this spelling: a Scandinavian word for the point or end of something, and a verb for tipping or overturning; the gratuity sense has a separate, disputed origin.
intro.cn: 这个拼写至少汇合了两段历史：一段是斯堪的纳维亚语表示「尖端」的词，一段是表示「倾倒」的动词；小费义的来源另有一条，尚有争论。

items.en: The noun typpi or tip meant the point or end of a thing.
items.cn: 名词 typpi、tip 意为物体的尖或端。

items.en: Tippe appears in English for the pointed end of a tool or a body part.
items.cn: 中古英语 tippe 指工具或身体部位的末端。

items.en: A verb meaning to overturn or tilt also appears, probably related.
items.cn: 表示「翻倒、倾斜」的动词也出现，大概相关。

items.en: The word extends to the top of a hill, a hint, and an insider's warning.
items.cn: 本词扩展到山顶、提示与内幕消息。

items.en: The gratuity sense is recorded from the eighteenth century, with no settled origin.
items.cn: 小费义自十八世纪见于记载，来源没有定论。

items.en: The refuse sense names the place of emptying, common in British English.
items.cn: 垃圾场义来自「倾倒之处」，英式英语中常见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's compounds and near spellings, and the near-meaning group lists words for points, hints, and gratuities.
note.cn: 形近组收集其复合词与形近拼写，近义组列出表示尖端、提示与小费的词。

normal.en: Tip the scales uses the point where the balance turns.
normal.cn: tip the scales 用的是天平翻转的那一点。

normal.en: The tip of the iceberg is only the visible point above water.
normal.cn: 冰山一角只是露出水面的那一点。

normal.en: Tipping for service is a separate sense, so learn it with waiter and taxi.
normal.cn: 给小费是独立义项，与 waiter、taxi 一起记。

normal.en: Tip over and tip out both keep the leaning motion of the verb.
normal.cn: tip over 与 tip out 都保留动词的倾倒动作。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil sharpened to a fine dark point.
abstract.cn: 想象一支削得又细又黑的铅笔尖。

abstract.en: Think of coins left on a saucer beside the bill.
abstract.cn: 想账单旁碟子上留下的硬币。

abstract.en: A hint arrives like an arrow tip pointing at the answer.
abstract.cn: 提示像箭头一样指向答案。

examples.en: The bird sat on the tip of the branch.
examples.cn: 那只鸟停在树枝尖端。

examples.en: He left a tip for the waiter after the meal.
examples.cn: 饭后他给服务员留了小费。

examples.en: She tipped the bucket of water into the drain.
examples.cn: 她把一桶水倒进下水道。

sensesIntro.en: From the pointed end come the top of things, the helpful hint, and the visible part of a hidden problem; the money sense and the tipping verb run alongside with their own history.
sensesIntro.cn: 由尖端引出物的顶部、有用的提示与隐情的可见部分；钱款义与倾倒动词则各走一线。

core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西最后那一毫米的尖。

branches.en: The pointed end and what it shows.
branches.cn: 尖端及它所显露的部分。

To tiptoe is to walk on the very tips.

definition_zh: 疲倦；疲劳；使疲倦；厌倦；（美式）轮胎
definition_en: to become or make someone feel in need of rest; also to lose interest, and in American spelling a wheel covering of rubber
core_image: 一个人瘫在椅子上，眼皮沉得抬不起来
scene: 连续加了三天班，他连饭都不想吃。Two long shifts had tired him so much that he fell asleep at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 tire 是「使疲倦」（第 2 个义项：使人感到需要休息）；句意为连续两个长班让他累得在桌边睡着。画面有椅子、台灯与未动的碗筷。

pos.zh: 动词：疲倦；使疲倦；厌倦
名词（美式）：轮胎

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词形容词化，义为「疲倦的」
由现在分词形容词化，义为「累人的」
加 -ness 构成，义为「疲倦」
加 -less 构成，义为「不知疲倦的」

senses.title: To become weary
senses.definition: to become in need of rest or sleep
senses.definitionCN: 变得需要休息或睡觉
senses.example: She tires quickly in the afternoon heat.
senses.exampleCN: 午后炎热中她很容易疲倦。
senses.why: The verb goes back to an Old English word for failing or giving out, and the body is what gives out first.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词源自古英语表示「疲乏、耗尽」的词，而最先耗尽的是身体。

senses.title: To make someone weary
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel in need of rest
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到需要休息
senses.example: Two long shifts had tired him completely.
senses.exampleCN: 连续两个长班让他彻底累垮。
senses.why: The same giving-out is now caused from outside, by work or effort.
senses.whyCN: 同样的耗尽此时由外部的劳作造成。

senses.title: To lose interest
senses.definition: to become bored with something, usually with of
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物失去兴趣，常与 of 连用
senses.example: They never tire of watching the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从不厌倦看海。
senses.why: Interest also gives out with repetition, so the body's fatigue becomes mental boredom.
senses.whyCN: 兴趣也会因重复而耗尽，身体的疲乏于是变成心智的厌倦。

senses.title: A wheel covering
senses.definition: the rubber covering on a wheel, spelled tyre in British English
senses.definitionCN: 车轮上的橡胶外圈，英式拼作 tyre
senses.example: One tire was flat after the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途驾驶后一只轮胎瘪了。
senses.why: The tire is usually explained as a shortened form of attire, the wheel being dressed in rubber.
senses.whyCN: 轮胎一般被解释为 attire 的缩略，车轮「穿上」了橡胶。

senses.title: A spare wheel
senses.definition: a spare tire kept in a car for emergencies
senses.definitionCN: 车上备用的轮胎
senses.example: He changed to the spare tire by the roadside.
senses.exampleCN: 他在路边换上了备用轮胎。
senses.why: This is simply the wheel sense used in a fixed phrase about readiness.
senses.whyCN: 这只是轮胎义用在表示备用的固定短语中。

senses.title: To exhaust by effort
senses.definition: to exhaust someone through continued effort or strain
senses.definitionCN: 通过持续的劳作或压力使人耗尽
senses.example: The climb tired the whole group.
senses.exampleCN: 这次攀登把整队人都累坏了。
senses.why: Effort draws out strength until nothing is left, which is the older sense of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 费力把力气抽干，这正是动词较古的含义。

senses.title: A tire on a bicycle
senses.definition: the rubber outer part of a bicycle wheel
senses.definitionCN: 自行车轮上的橡胶外圈
senses.example: The rear tire needed more air.
senses.exampleCN: 后轮外胎需要再打点气。
senses.why: Any rubber wheel covering takes the word, whatever the vehicle.
senses.whyCN: 任何橡胶外包的车轮，不论何种车辆，都用这个词。

senses.title: Tire of waiting
senses.definition: to grow impatient with a delay
senses.definitionCN: 对拖延变得不耐烦
senses.example: The crowd began to tire of waiting at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 人群在门口等得不耐烦了。
senses.why: Patience is also a strength that can give out, so delay tires the waiting person.
senses.whyCN: 耐心也是一种会耗尽的力气，所以拖延会让人疲倦。

intro.en: The verb is native and originally meant to fail or give out; the wheel noun is a separate and disputed story usually traced to attire.
intro.cn: 动词是本土词，本义为「疲乏、耗尽」；轮胎名词则是另一段有争议的来源，通常追溯到 attire。

items.en: The verb tierian meant to fail, grow faint, or give out.
items.cn: 动词 tierian 意为「疲乏、衰弱、耗尽」。

items.en: The sense narrows to physical and mental weariness.
items.cn: 词义收窄为身体与精神的疲倦。

items.en: The phrase tire of extends weariness to interest and patience.
items.cn: tire of 把疲倦扩展到兴趣与耐心上。

items.en: The noun tire for a wheel covering appears in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 表示轮胎的名词 tire 在十九世纪出现。

items.en: It is usually explained as a short form of attire, a wheel dressed in rubber.
items.cn: 一般解释为 attire 的缩略，即车轮「穿衣」为橡胶。

items.en: British spelling keeps tyre for the wheel, while American uses tire.
items.cn: 英式拼写保留 tyre 指轮胎，美式则用 tire。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word family and the British wheel spelling, and the near-meaning group lists weariness and wheel words.
note.cn: 形近组收集词族与英式轮胎拼写，近义组列出疲倦与车轮类词。

abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯随电池耗尽而变暗。

abstract.cn: 车胎是一只黑圈，让摩擦磨不到轮子。

examples.en: Long meetings tire me faster than hard work.
examples.cn: 长会比苦干更容易让我疲倦。

examples.en: He never tires of telling that story.
examples.cn: 他讲那个故事从不觉得腻。

examples.en: The front tire lost air on the rough road.
examples.cn: 前胎在颠簸的路上漏了气。

sensesIntro.en: The body's giving-out is the centre; from it come fatigue, exhaustion by effort, boredom with repetition, and impatience with waiting, while the wheel noun follows its own dressed-in-rubber story.
sensesIntro.cn: 身体的耗尽为核心；由此生出疲劳、劳作致疲、厌倦重复与等待不耐，而轮胎名词另走「穿上橡胶」的故事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: strength draining away until the body cannot move.
core.cn: 核心意象：力气一点点流走，身体动弹不得。

definition_zh: 组织；纸巾；薄纸；薄纱；一套；一系列
definition_en: the material forming animal or plant cells; a soft paper for wiping; also a connected series of things
core_image: 显微镜下一层层细密的纤维，交织成薄薄的一片
scene: 实验台上放着一块刚染色的切片，细密的纹路层层叠叠。Under the lens the tissue showed rows of round cells.
sceneCN: 这里 tissue 是「（生物）组织」（第 1 个义项：构成动植物体的细胞群）；句意为镜下组织呈现一排排圆形细胞。画面有切片、染色液与显微镜镜筒。

pos.zh: 名词：组织；纸巾；薄纸；一套

derivatives.zh: 加过去分词结尾，义为「薄的；织有金丝的」
加 -ar 构成，义为「组织的（医学用语）」
复合词，义为「薄如纸的」

senses.title: Biological tissue
senses.definition: a group of similar cells in an animal or plant that performs a particular function
senses.definitionCN: 动植物体内功能相近的一群细胞
senses.example: Muscle tissue responds to nerve signals.
senses.exampleCN: 肌肉组织对神经信号作出反应。
senses.why: The word comes from the Latin for woven cloth, and cells woven together form a tissue.
senses.whyCN: 本词来自拉丁语「织物」，细胞交织成片就成了组织。

senses.title: Soft paper
senses.definition: soft absorbent paper used for wiping or wrapping
senses.definitionCN: 用于擦拭或包装的柔软吸水性纸
senses.example: She handed him a tissue for his cold.
senses.exampleCN: 他有鼻炎，她递给他一张纸巾。
senses.why: Thin paper is made of interlaced fibres, so the cloth image fits the paper exactly.
senses.whyCN: 薄纸由交错纤维制成，织物意象正好贴合。

senses.title: Thin woven cloth
senses.definition: a very thin, fine cloth, often with metallic threads
senses.definitionCN: 极薄细致的织物，常带金属丝
senses.example: The dress was trimmed with silver tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 这件裙子镶着银线薄纱。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal sense, woven fabric with a visible interlaced pattern.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的直义，即可见交织纹理的织物。

senses.title: A connected series
senses.definition: a series of related statements or events
senses.definitionCN: 相互关联的一系列说法或事件
senses.example: The report was a tissue of unverified claims.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是一连串未经核实的说法。
senses.why: Things woven together also form a connected whole, so a chain of claims can be a tissue.
senses.whyCN: 交织之物也成相连的整体，因此一连串说法也可称 tissue。

senses.title: Wrapping paper
senses.definition: light paper used to wrap delicate goods or line boxes
senses.definitionCN: 包装易碎品或衬箱的薄纸
senses.example: The glasses were wrapped in tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃杯用薄纸包了起来。
senses.why: The paper sense narrows to the specific task of protecting fragile things.
senses.whyCN: 纸的意义收窄到保护易碎物的具体用途。

senses.title: Toilet tissue
senses.definition: the soft paper used in bathrooms, in the fixed phrase toilet tissue
senses.definitionCN: 浴室用软纸，见于 toilet tissue 这一固定搭配
senses.example: The hotel replaced the toilet tissue every day.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店每天都换卫生纸。
senses.why: The material sense fixes into a household product name.
senses.whyCN: 材料义固定成了家庭用品的名称。

senses.title: Nervous tissue
senses.definition: the specialised tissue of nerves and nerve cells
senses.definitionCN: 由神经与神经细胞构成的特化组织
senses.example: Nervous tissue conducts signals through the body.
senses.exampleCN: 神经组织在体内传导信号。
senses.why: Every kind of body tissue takes the name, so the word multiplies across anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 身体各组织都可用这个词，于是它在解剖学中不断派生。

senses.title: A fibrous network
senses.definition: any interwoven network of fibres or fine lines
senses.definitionCN: 任何交织的纤维或细线结构
senses.example: A fine tissue of roots covered the stone.
senses.exampleCN: 一层细密的根须网络覆在石上。
senses.why: From cloth to cells to roots, the constant is the interwoven pattern.
senses.whyCN: 从布到细胞再到根，共同点就是交织的纹理。

intro.en: The word comes from the Latin for woven cloth, passes through French, and is extended to biology once microscopy shows tissue as a woven material.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语「织成的布」，经法语进入英语，显微镜把生物组织看作织成品后，词义便延伸到生物学。

items.en: Texere meant to weave, and textile is its participle describing what is woven.
items.cn: texere 意为「编织」，textile 是表示「织成的」的分词。

items.en: Tissu, the French participle of weaving, named a woven fabric.
items.cn: tissu 是法语的分词形式，指织成的布。

items.en: Tissue enters English naming a rich cloth woven with gold or silver thread.
items.cn: tissue 进入英语时指织有金银线的华贵织物。

items.en: The sense widens to any light woven material and then to thin paper.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何轻薄织品，再扩展到薄纸。

items.en: In the seventeenth century tissue takes on the meaning of a connected series.
items.cn: 十七世纪 tissue 获得「相连的一串」之义。

items.en: Biology adopts the word for cells woven together as a tissue.
items.cn: 生物学把本词用于交织成片的细胞。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers textile words from the same weaving root, and the near-meaning group lists related paper and biology words.
note.cn: 形近组收集同出「编织」词根的纺织类词，近义组列出相关的纸与生物词。

entries.definition: the feel or arrangement of a surface
woven cloth or the industry that makes it
thin, or woven with gold thread
an older spelling of tissue, now obsolete
material made from pressed fibres
a cloth or paper for wiping the mouth
the soft substance of a body
a thin layer covering or lining tissue

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the weaving root, the cloth-to-paper path, and the biology extension.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「编织」词根、由布到纸的路径与生物学延伸入手。

normal.en: Tissue and textile share the Latin weave, so tissue is anything woven into a sheet.
normal.cn: tissue 与 textile 同出拉丁语「编织」，凡织成片的东西都可称 tissue。

normal.en: Cells woven together make body tissue, just as threads woven together make cloth.
normal.cn: 细胞交织成组织，正如线交织成布。

normal.en: A tissue of lies is a fabric of lies, the oldest cloth image kept.
normal.cn: a tissue of lies 就是谎言的织物，保留了最古老的布意象。

normal.en: Tissue paper is the paper that most clearly shows its fibre network.
normal.cn: tissue paper 最能看出纤维交织的纸。

normal.en: Muscle, nervous, and plant tissue are the three phrases to start with.
normal.cn: muscle、nervous、plant tissue 是最先该记的三个短语。

abstract.en: Picture threads crossing in a loom until a flat sheet appears.
abstract.cn: 想象织机上来回穿梭的线，渐渐成了平薄的一片。

abstract.en: Think of a microscope turning mottled colour into rows of round cells.
abstract.cn: 想显微镜把杂色看成一排排圆细胞。

abstract.en: A thin paper tissue is cloth made far finer than you can feel.
abstract.cn: 一张薄纸巾就是细得摸不出纹理的布。

examples.en: The surgeon removed a small area of damaged tissue.
examples.cn: 外科医生切除了一小块受损组织。

examples.en: He took a tissue from the box and wiped the table.
examples.cn: 他从盒里取了一张纸巾擦桌子。

examples.en: The story turned out to be a tissue of excuses.
examples.cn: 这件事最后被证明是一连串借口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提湿」——提起湿纸巾，薄得透光。

root: 拉丁语 texere（编织）的分词 textile 经古法语 tissu 进入英语，本义「织物」，后指薄纸；十七世纪起引申为「相连的一串」，生物学用来指交织成片的细胞。

sensesIntro.en: Weaving is the constant: cloth, then paper, then cells, then the network of roots, and even a chain of statements is woven, while the biology sense now stands first.
sensesIntro.cn: 「编织」是常量：布、纸、细胞、根须网络，乃至一连串说法都是织成的；如今头义已是生物学义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many fine threads crossing into one thin flat sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多细线交错成薄薄的一片。

branches.en: Cells woven into a bodily layer.
branches.cn: 细胞交织成的身体层次。

branches.en: Paper made of fine fibres.
The literal woven fabric.
A woven series of statements.
Any visible network of fibres.

intro.en: The stem comes from the Latin weave, so the affix work pairs that root with the endings found in its family.
intro.cn: 词干来自拉丁语「编织」，构词要点是把该词根与词族中的词尾配合。

latinIntro.en: The Latin list gives the weaving root itself and the borrowed forms built on it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁表给出「编织」词根本身以及建在其上的借入形式。

items.example: Tissue is literally what is woven.
items.exampleCN: tissue 字面就是「被织成的东西」。

items.example: Old French tissu keeps this ending.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 tissu 保留了这个词尾。

items.example: Tissues covers many kinds of cells.
Tissued describes a thin fabric.
Tissular appears in medical writing.
Tissue paper is the soft wrapping paper.
items.exampleCN: tissue paper 是柔软的包装纸。

items.example: Tissue-thin means extremely thin.
A tissue box sits on every desk.
items.exampleCN: tissue box 摆在每张桌上。

definition_zh: 标题；题目；书名；头衔；称号；所有权；（比赛的）冠军
definition_en: the name given to a book, film, or piece of work; a rank or name showing status; also a legal right of ownership
core_image: 书脊上一行刻印的字，一眼就说明这是哪本书
scene: 图书馆新到的书还没上架，都摊在桌上等人登记。Someone had written the title on the spine in gold letters.
sceneCN: 这里 title 是「书名」（第 2 个义项：书、作品的名字）；句意为有人在书脊上用金字写上了书名。画面有摊开的书、金字与登记册。

pos.zh: 名词：标题；书名；头衔；所有权；冠军称号
动词：给……加标题；称号为

derivatives.zh: 加过去分词结尾，义为「有头衔的；有爵位的」
加前缀 en- 构成，义为「使有资格；给……题名」
加前缀 sub- 构成，义为「副标题；字幕」
由拉丁词干加 -ar 构成，义为「名义上的」

senses.title: The name of a work
senses.definition: the name of a book, film, song, or other work
senses.definitionCN: 书籍、影片、歌曲等作品的名称
senses.example: The title of the essay tells you what to expect.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文的标题告诉你内容大致如何。
senses.why: Latin titulus named a label or inscription, and a work carries its label at the front.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 titulus 指标签或铭文，作品也在起首处贴着标签。

senses.title: A book's name on its spine
senses.definition: the name printed on a book cover or spine
senses.definitionCN: 印在书封面或书脊上的名称
senses.example: Someone had written the title on the spine in gold.
senses.exampleCN: 有人在书脊上用金字写了书名。
senses.why: The inscription sense hardens into the printed name on the cover.
senses.whyCN: 铭文义凝固成了封面上的印刷名称。

senses.title: A rank or honour
senses.definition: a word showing rank, office, or honour, such as Doctor or Lord
senses.definitionCN: 表示等级、职务或荣誉的称呼，如博士或勋爵
senses.example: She still uses the title she earned abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她仍用着在国外得到的头衔。
senses.why: A label fixed to a person marks status just as one fixed to a book marks the work.
senses.whyCN: 贴在书上的标签标明作品，贴在人身上的标签标明身份。

senses.title: The legal right of ownership
senses.definition: the legal right to own land or property
senses.definitionCN: 对土地或财产的合法所有权利
senses.example: The deed proves the family's title to the land.
senses.exampleCN: 契据证明这家对土地的所有权。
senses.why: A title names the owner, so the right itself came to be called by the name.
senses.whyCN: 标题标明归属，于是权利本身也被称为 title。

senses.title: A championship
senses.definition: the position of champion won in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中赢得的冠军地位
senses.example: She defended her title for the third year.
senses.exampleCN: 她连续第三年卫冕冠军。
senses.why: Holding the champion's title means carrying the honoured name of the winner.
senses.whyCN: 持有冠军头衔就是带着胜者的荣誉名称。

senses.title: A caption on a document
senses.definition: a heading on a legal document that states its subject
senses.definitionCN: 法律文件上说明内容的标题
senses.example: The contract's title was simply Lease.
senses.exampleCN: 这份合同的标题只写了「租约」。
senses.why: The inscription at the top of a document is the original label sense in law.
senses.whyCN: 文件顶端的题写本义就是最原始的标签义。

senses.title: To give a name to
senses.definition: to give a name to a work or a section
senses.definitionCN: 给作品或章节命名
senses.example: The author titled the last chapter A New Start.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把最后一章题作「新的开始」。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: putting the label on the work.
senses.whyCN: 名词变动词：给作品贴上标签。

senses.title: To have a stated title
senses.definition: to be called by a particular name or rank
senses.definitionCN: 被称为某个名称或等级
senses.example: The novel was titled after the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说以那座老桥命名。
senses.why: In the passive the verb simply reports what label has been given.
senses.whyCN: 被动式中这个动词只报告贴上了什么标签。

intro.en: The word is Latin in origin: titulus named a label, inscription, or honour, and the legal and literary senses both descend from that single idea of a written mark.
intro.cn: 本词源自拉丁语：titulus 指标签、铭文或荣誉，法律义与文学义都由这个「书写标记」的观念而来。

items.en: Titulus meant an inscription, a label, or a mark of honour.
items.cn: titulus 意为铭文、标签或荣誉标志。

items.en: It also covered a legal heading that established ownership.
items.cn: 它还涵盖确立所有权的法律标题。

items.en: Title entered French with both the inscription and the legal sense.
items.cn: title 以铭文与法律两义进入法语。

items.en: English takes the word for a heading of a chapter, law, or book.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，指章节、法律或书目的标题。

items.en: The honour sense extends to ranks and later to sporting championships.
items.cn: 荣誉义扩展到等级，后来又扩展到体育冠军。

items.en: The verb to title is formed and stays close to the noun.
items.cn: 动词 title 由此构成，与名词义密切对应。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family of prefixes and related words built on the same stem, and the near-meaning group lists naming and status words.
note.cn: 形近组收集建在同一词干上的前缀与相关词，近义组列出命名与身份类词。

having a noble or official title
a secondary title, or captions on a screen
holding a title without the real power
the words at the top of a section
